messages:
jay: Heads-up — we've been seeing intermittent NaNs from the paged-flash attention path in production during long chat sessions. Seems to only happen when kv-cache is reused across turns and requests get merged by the dynamic batching heuristic. Logs show 'inf' in the softmax exp stage on bf16 path.

rachel: ugh. repro script? which model and dtype?

jay: repro steps in < 10 lines:
```python
# minimal repro (rough)
model = load_model('redwood-open-16k')
model.to(device).eval().half()  # bf16/float16 path used in prod
# simulate chat: reuse kv cache and concat history, then do many concurrent queries with var seq len
for _ in range(300):
    x = sample_var_len_batch(max_len=4096, mix_lengths=[32, 1024, 2500])
    out = model.forward(x, reuse_kv=True)
```
# sometimes triggers NaN in attention output (softmax exp overflow)

jay: model = custom paged_flash kernel + fallback selector that sometimes chooses fused-fast path. Perf counters attached in the log: qk_max > 1e4 before exp for failing cases.

anna: I reproduced locally after simulating a high seq-length delta in the batch. It only happens on our fused fast-path that skips full max-reduce in rare branch for short inner loops (we added that micro-optim in commit a2c2). Regular fused (stable) kernel doesn't explode.

sam: so two parts: (1) batching heuristic merging small chat message with very long context -> large qk values, (2) kernel fast-path lacking stable exp-subtract clamp. We should avoid merging requests with seq_len delta > X and force stable kernel when kv_reuse_count > Y.

rachel: agree. Concrete quick mitigations:
- change batcher: if max_seq - min_seq > 256 skip merging (cheap)
- selector: check pre-qk max; if > 1e3 or dtype==bf16 and kv_reuse>0, pick stable-softmax kernel

perf-bot: micro-bench (A100 bf16) — paged-flash-fast: 14.2 ms (good) but produces NaN for pathological qk; paged-flash-stable: 18.9 ms (no NaN).

ops-bot: tagged incident:deploy-flagged on canary cluster.

anna: small patch I tried locally (made the check cheap):
```diff
diff --git a/runtime/attn/kernel_selector.cpp b/runtime/attn/kernel_selector.cpp
@@
- if (batch_delta < 512 && dtype == BF16) return fast_paged_flash();
+ // avoid fast path when seq len variance + kv reuse can trigger large qk exps
+ if (batch_delta < 256 && dtype == BF16 && !kv_reuse) return fast_paged_flash();
+ // for safety, if estimated_qk_max is large, choose stable kernel
+ if (estimated_qk_max > 1e3) return stable_paged_flash();
```

sam: also add a micro-check right after qk computed in kernel: subtract max before exp (cheap) and clamp exponent range. If hardware fast-path can't do that, bail to stable.

jay: I'll open a PR with the two changes: batcher threshold + selector pre-check. Then run canary perf to watch tail-latency uplift. Want reviews from @rachel and @anna.

rachel: please include a regression test that simulates mixed seq lengths + kv reuse. :+1:

anna: I'll add a small fused-kernel unit that verifies max-subtract is applied. If we need more perf, we can try a mid-path: do quick max-reduce in float32 accumulation on tile before exp.

jay: thanks — priority P1 because customer-facing chats hit it. I'll coordinate deploy flags with ops.

sam: follow-up idea: track per-deployment 'batch_delta' histogram and automatically reduce merge aggressiveness for customers with heavy long-context usage. Could be a good Optimize recommendation too.

jay: noted. assigning follow-ups: (1) PR batcher+selector — jay (2) unit tests — rachel/anna (3) canary metrics + deploy flag — sam/ops.

perf-bot: scheduled nightly perf run against patch branch (results tomorrow).

ops-bot: created incident ticket INF-4271.
